text:
jen (customer): hi, seeing an odd billing + streaming issue. Using SSE to stream completions. midway through stream we get a 429 and the connection closes. client reconnects and we see duplicated partial tokens and the ledger shows two charges for the same user session.

jen (customer): reproducible with a simple EventSource client, no retries configured beyond default. example client:
```js
const src = new EventSource('https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams?model=rw-large&session=widget-77');
src.onmessage = (e) => console.log('msg', e.data);
src.onerror = (e) => console.log('sse error', e);
```
We see ~120 tokens then an error event with HTTP 429. After reconnect we get ~30 more tokens, but final text is incomplete and the dashboard shows two billable rows.

sophia (support): sorry about that. can you post the raw response headers for the 429 and any request ids? also confirm whether you include any session-identifying query param or header.

jen (customer): headers captured by tcpdump when 429 happened:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Date: Wed, 03 Dec 2025 09:11:40 GMT
X-Req-Id: rwd-a7f3c9d2
X-RateLimit-Limit: 120000
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 3
Content-Type: text/event-stream
Retry-After: 3
```
We didn't set any explicit session header, only `session=widget-77` in the query string.

raja (oncall): thanks — initial read: the runtime currently enforces quota checks per HTTP request. For SSE that means each reconnect looks like a new request and the allocator may provision additional token quota. If a mid-stream quota check fails (window boundary or burst limit), runtime sends 429 and closes the stream. The client reconnects with a new request id and allocator may count the newly allocated tokens separately, which leads to double-counting in billing if we don't reconcile by session.

alex (eng-runtime): adding logs for rwd-a7f3c9d2 from our side:
```
[09:11:36.890] rwd-a7f3c9d2 session=widget-77 auth=ok alloc=5000 tokens_emitted=118
[09:11:39.995] rwd-a7f3c9d2 quota-check remaining=0 -> respond 429 cause=burst-throttle
[09:11:39.996] rwd-a7f3c9d2 stream:event error payload="rate_limited"
[09:11:39.997] rwd-a7f3c9d2 connection: teardown
[09:11:40.210] rwd-a7f3c9d2-reconn session=widget-77 auth=ok alloc=2500 tokens_emitted=28
```
Note the reconnection has a distinct request id `-reconn` and a separate allocation line. billing pipeline currently tracks allocations by request id and doesn't dedupe on session.

sophia (support): two immediate things you can try: 1) Add a stable header like `X-Stream-Session: <uuid>` on the initial handshake and reconnects so we can map reconnects to the original session server-side. 2) Reduce automatic reconnect aggressiveness on the client (EventSource `retry` backoff) so you don't immediately re-open and trigger allocation. Both should reduce duplicate charges while we fix infra.

jen (customer): can you confirm whether a query `session` param is sufficient? we're already sending `session=widget-77` but it didn't prevent the double-charge.

raja (oncall): query params can be used but they are less reliable if proxies or caches mutate URLs. Headers are preferable. We'll make the runtime treat a matching `X-Stream-Session` as the canonical session identifier and avoid re-charging within a short grace window.

alex (eng-runtime): proposed short-term patch: when a stream handshake includes `X-Stream-Session`, mark allocation with a `stream_session_id` and keep allocations for that id open for 90s. If a reconnect occurs with same id, do not create a new allocation; instead resume accounting against the existing allocation. This requires minimal ledger changes and should prevent 2x billing for reconnects. We'll also alter mid-stream quota behavior to prefer failing gracefully (emit event error but do not allocate new tokens on reconnect).

billing-bot: auto-note: created ticket BILL-1249 to reconcile ledger entries for rwd-a7f3c9d2. Put provisional credit flag on customer account pending root-cause.

alex (eng-runtime): longer term: move billing join key from request_id -> stream_session_id for streaming endpoints; backfill historical streams where we can. Also we'll add an indicator in the emitted stream events `event: meta\ndata: {"stream_session_id":"...","tokens_emitted":N}` to make reconciliation easier for customers.

sophia (support): jen, we can issue a one-off credit while eng delivers the hotfix if the ledger shows duplicate allocations tied to reconnects. please DM me the two request ids and we'll start the reconcile.

jen (customer): thanks. i'll add `X-Stream-Session` and test. curious whether rate-limit headers like `Retry-After` should be handled specially by the client to avoid immediate reconnects; looks like `Retry-After` was present.

raja (oncall): yes, honoring `Retry-After` can reduce thrashing. EventSource default reconnect behavior ignores `Retry-After`, so we recommend either a custom SSE client or a small wrapper that reads the header from the initial disconnect event (if provided) and backs off. We'll add guidance to our docs.

alex (eng-runtime): timeline: hotfix to make allocations session-scoped and to treat reconnects idempotently planned for canary within 48 hours. billing team will run a reconcile job for the affected request ids.

jen (customer): appreciated. leaving logs and req ids in a DM. will test with `X-Stream-Session` and report back.

sophia (support): thanks all, marking this triaged -> eng-runtime + billing. we'll follow up here when fix is deployed and credits applied. :white_check_mark:
